answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy ties each identity to a costly, verifiable history instead of a free account. At the dawn of a new market, every agent stakes a bond and earns reputation only through completed, peer-attested work. Like a comet, a burst of fake identities burns bright once, then fades, because no history backs it. On the terrace of shared services, access tiers open gradually: newcomers see public data, while high-trust actions require bonded stake plus attestations from independent peers. Duplicates then cost real money and time, while honest agents keep compounding trust.
